content.text:
Found it. You're in an SSH session (`SSH_TTY=/dev/pts/0`), so this branch is live:

`home-manager/nvim/lua/config/clipboard.lua:29-32`
```lua
paste = {
    ['+'] = function() return vim.fn.getreg('0', 1, true) end,
```

**Register `0` is the yank-only register.** `dd`, `d`, `x`, `c` never touch it — they write to `"` and shift `1`–`9`. And line 40 forces `clipboard=unnamedplus` in *every* branch, so plain `p` reads `+` → that stub → register `0` → the last thing you **yanked**, ignoring everything you deleted.

Copy works because OSC 52 genuinely writes to your local terminal's clipboard (that's why ctrl+shift+v is correct). There's no read path — most terminals won't answer an OSC 52 read — so that stub is a fake, and it's lying about which register it fakes.

Fix — keep registers native over SSH, mirror yanks/deletes out via OSC 52:

```lua
elseif vim.env.SSH_TTY then
	-- Remote: registers stay local so dd/yy/p behave normally;
	-- mirror them to the local terminal's clipboard via OSC 52 (write-only).
	local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
	vim.opt.clipboard = ""
	vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("TextYankPost", {
		callback = function()
			osc52.copy("+")(vim.v.event.regcontents, vim.v.event.regtype)
		end,
	})
else
	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamed,unnamedplus"
end
```

Plus move line 40's `:append("unnamedplus")` into the mac branch, otherwise it re-breaks it.

Skipped: real OSC 52 paste (`osc52.paste`) — needs terminal read-clipboard consent through tmux, blocks on timeout, and ctrl+shift+v already covers pasting from the local machine. Want me to apply it?

content.text:
Confirmed — three facts settle it:

- `tmux show-environment -g` still holds `SSH_TTY=/dev/pts/0`, frozen from whenever this tmux server was first started over SSH.
- `update-environment` (tmux's default list) refreshes `SSH_CONNECTION`, `DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` — but **not `SSH_TTY`**. So your newest nvim pane got a fresh `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1` and `DISPLAY=:0` (you're local, exactly as you said) while still carrying the stale `SSH_TTY`.
- `clipboard.lua:19` branches on `vim.env.SSH_TTY` → takes the OSC 52 path anyway.

Copy works because tmux `set-clipboard on` forwards the OSC 52 write to kitty. Paste is the stub returning register `0` — the yank-only register, which `dd`/`d`/`c` never touch — so `p` replays your last **yank**.

Fixing both halves:

input.content:
-- Clipboard configuration
--
-- Let Neovim autodetect the provider. It already picks pbcopy/pbpaste on macOS,
-- wl-copy/wl-paste under Wayland, xclip/xsel under X11, and falls back to OSC 52
-- when there is genuinely no local clipboard (real SSH).
--
-- Do NOT branch on $SSH_TTY: tmux does not list it in update-environment, so a
-- tmux server first started over SSH leaks a stale SSH_TTY into every pane
-- forever, and local sessions get misdetected as remote.
vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"

content.text:
Verified read-only (didn't touch your clipboard): with `SSH_TTY` unset, `vim.g.clipboard` is `nil` — no override — and `getreg('+')` returns your real clipboard content. The Wayland provider works fine; the config was just routing around it.

To apply:

```sh
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .    # from the repo
tmux set-environment -gr SSH_TTY       # drop the stale var from the running server
```

The `set-environment` line only affects **new** panes — this tmux server has carried that variable since it started, and existing panes keep their inherited copy. Open a fresh pane and restart nvim there to test; `dd` then `p` should give you the deleted line.

Skipped: the OSC 52 copy path entirely — you have a real Wayland clipboard on lucie, and nvim re-adds OSC 52 by itself if you ever run it on a genuinely remote box.

Worth knowing: that stale `SSH_TTY` is also why your prompt has `P9K_SSH=1` — powerlevel10k thinks you're remote for the same reason. The tmux fix clears that too.

content.text:
Your hypothesis is right, and it's more precisely right than what I said. The session env proves it:

```
-SSH_CONNECTION          ← tmux marked it for REMOVAL: the last client to attach was local
DISPLAY=:0
WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1
```

tmux has already worked out you're local — it cleared `SSH_CONNECTION` on attach because that var *is* in `update-environment`. But `SSH_TTY` and `SSH_CLIENT` aren't in that list, so they're absent from the session env and every new pane falls through to the **global** env, which still holds `SSH_TTY=/dev/pts/0` and `SSH_CLIENT=10.100.0.101...` from the day the server was started over SSH.

p10k then re-derives it fresh every time (`internal/p10k.zsh:8483`):

```zsh
if [[ -n $SSH_CLIENT || -n $SSH_TTY || -n $SSH_CONNECTION ]]; then
  P9K_SSH=1
```

Notably it isn't a remembered verdict — the cache at line 8480 is keyed to `$TTY`, and it already invalidated: your global env has `_P9K_SSH_TTY=/dev/pts/0` while this pane is `pts/20`. So p10k *did* recheck, and the stale vars fooled it again.

One correction to what I told you: adding only `SSH_TTY` to `update-environment` would not have fixed the prompt, since `SSH_CLIENT` alone still trips that condition. Both are needed:

input.old_string:
# tmux's default update-environment refreshes SSH_CONNECTION but not SSH_TTY, so
# a server first started over SSH leaks a stale SSH_TTY into every later pane.
set -ga update-environment "SSH_TTY"
input.new_string:
# tmux's default update-environment refreshes SSH_CONNECTION but not SSH_TTY or
# SSH_CLIENT, so a server first started over SSH leaks those two into every later
# pane forever - which makes nvim and powerlevel10k think a local session is remote.
set -ga update-environment "SSH_TTY SSH_CLIENT"

Immediate cleanup for the already-running server (survives until you rebuild):

```sh
tmux set-environment -gr SSH_TTY
tmux set-environment -gr SSH_CLIENT
```

New panes only — this pane keeps its inherited copy.

This won't break the real case: when you genuinely attach over SSH, `update-environment` copies the live values in from that client, which is what it's for.

git add home-manager/nvim/lua/config/clipboard.lua home-manager/tmux/tmux.conf && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
nvim,tmux: paste from the real clipboard on local sessions

A tmux server first started over SSH keeps SSH_TTY and SSH_CLIENT in its
global environment forever - update-environment refreshes SSH_CONNECTION
but not those two - so every later pane inherits them and a local session
looks remote.

clipboard.lua branched on $SSH_TTY and so took the OSC 52 path, whose
paste handler returned register 0. That register only ever holds the last
yank, so p after dd pasted the wrong text. Drop the branching entirely and
let Neovim autodetect the provider (pbcopy on macOS, wl-copy under Wayland,
xclip under X11, OSC 52 only when there is no local clipboard), and add the
two leaking vars to update-environment - which also stops powerlevel10k
showing an SSH prompt on a local session.
EOF
git log --oneline -1 && git status --short
